title: Design and Develop a Modular Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) Platform for Smart Warehouse Automation
description:
• Description Research and develop a concept design of a warehouse automation robot platform and a modular attachment for it, using Autodesk Fusion. Re-imagine their design and optimize for additive manufacturing.
The idea submission consists of two mandatory concept development challenges:
Part A – Universal Mobile Robot Platform (AGV/AMR Base)
Develop a concept design of a universal Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) / Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) chassis that serves as a common mobile platform for warehouse automation. The platform should support multiple interchangeable attachments while considering structural integrity, payload capacity, weight reduction, modularity, manufacturability, and ease of maintenance.
Part B – Modular Functional Attachments Develop a concept design for any one modular attachment that integrates with the universal platform to perform specific warehouse automation tasks. Example attachments include bin handling, pallet handling, conveyor transfer, robotic picking, inventory scanning, inspection, or any other innovative warehouse automation module.
Students should use Fusion features such as Generative Design, Topology Optimization, Additive Build, and Simulation. The redesigned components should demonstrate innovation, enhanced functionality, improved efficiency, and optimized material usage while being suitable for additive manufacturing.
• Participation Guidelines For Idea Submission
• Each student team should submit Fusion public link of the Conceptual Design as described in Part-A and Part-B of the above problem statement and a PowerPoint presentation (5-7 Slides).
• Designs should be created using ONLY Autodesk Fusion and not copied or taken from any other source.
• AI Generated content is NOT ALLOWED.
For Grand Finale*: Students must use Autodesk Fusion to design, and 3D print final design of specific components (scaled down to machine size) within the given time period and present the following to the jury members:
• PPT explaining the final project
• Final 3D prints
• Public link of the design
• Rendered images NOTE: *Grand Finale details to be revealed on competition day.
• Attach Marking Criteria Table here*
• Faculty (SIH SPOC) Form Teams choosing to submit idea for Autodesk’s problem statement are required to request their faculty (SIH SPOC) to fill this 'Mandatory Form'.
• Autodesk Fusion
• Autodesk Fusion combines Additive Manufacturing (3D printing) capabilities with Generative Design features. It allows users to optimize designs for 3D printing, generate support structures, and explore numerous design options using algorithms. This integration enables the creation of complex and optimized parts using 3D printing technologies.
• Students and educators can click Here to get FREE access to Fusion.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, generative, autonomous applied to a robotics and drones problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Robotics and Drones. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on integration. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Modular Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) Platform for Smart Warehouse Automation (Autodesk Fusion Design Challenge)

overview.in_plain_terms: Design (not build) a modular warehouse robot chassis and one interchangeable attachment, like a bin-handler or scanner arm, using Autodesk Fusion's generative design and manufacturing-optimization tools, as a concept submission rather than a working robot.
overview.why_it_matters: This is a design-engineering challenge testing genuine manufacturability and modularity thinking, not a software build, the value is in demonstrating real design-for-manufacturing skill using professional CAD tools.
pain_points: Warehouse automation platforms often aren't designed with true modularity or manufacturability in mind.
Custom robot chassis designs are often not optimized for weight, structural integrity, or additive manufacturing.
No standard, reusable base platform approach is demonstrated for multiple attachment types.
overview.background: This is an Autodesk-sponsored concept design challenge, not a software build, requiring use of Autodesk Fusion for generative design, topology optimization, and additive manufacturing workflows.
overview.whats_being_asked: A concept design (via Autodesk Fusion) of a universal AMR/AGV chassis platform plus one modular functional attachment, optimized using generative design and topology optimization for additive manufacturing.
expected_solution: Universal mobile robot chassis concept design.
One modular attachment concept (bin handling, picking, scanning, etc.).
Generative design and topology optimization applied.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: This PS is a design/CAD submission format, not a working software or hardware build, evaluation criteria differ fundamentally from the coding-hackathon PS elsewhere in this dataset.
analysis.invention_effort_note: The deliverable is a concept design plus documentation, not a functioning robot, effort goes into CAD modeling and design optimization within Fusion, not coding or physical fabrication.

competitive_landscape.level: Low crowding among typical hackathon teams
competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine CAD/mechanical-design skill and access to Autodesk Fusion specifically, a different skillset than most PS in this dataset, draws a distinct pool of participants.

innovation.note: Innovation here is judged on design creativity and manufacturing optimization thinking, not algorithmic novelty.

invention.note: Effort is judged on genuine use of Fusion's generative design/topology optimization tools, not code complexity.

technical_feasibility.note: Fully achievable as a concept design submission within 36 hours for a team with real Fusion/CAD experience; not achievable at all without it.

impact_and_benefits.note: Impact here is about demonstrating genuine design-for-manufacturing capability, not deployed real-world impact.

architecture.note: Not applicable in the software-architecture sense, this is a mechanical design deliverable.

overall_verdict.reasoning: This PS should only be attempted by a team with genuine Autodesk Fusion experience or strong CAD/mechanical design aptitude, it's not adaptable to a general software team's skillset. If your team has this capability, it's a genuinely completable, well-specified design challenge.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very clearly specified deliverable structure (Part A chassis, Part B attachment) with explicit tool requirements (Generative Design, Topology Optimization, Additive Build).
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A team without real CAD/mechanical design experience, specifically in Autodesk Fusion, cannot meaningfully attempt this PS regardless of general coding skill.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm real, hands-on Autodesk Fusion experience on your team, specifically with generative design and topology optimization features, before considering this PS at all.

idea_0_4: Confirm team Fusion proficiency; if none, do not pursue this PS.
Sketch your chassis concept and attachment concept on paper first, considering modularity and manufacturability.
Split: one person on Part A (chassis), one on Part B (attachment), collaborating on the shared interface design.
prototype_4_22: Model your chassis concept in Fusion, applying generative design/topology optimization for weight reduction and structural integrity.
Model your chosen attachment concept with a clear, functional interface to the chassis.
Iterate on manufacturability considerations for additive manufacturing (overhangs, support structures, print orientation).
integration_22_30: Ensure the chassis and attachment interface genuinely and correctly, not just visually.
Run simulation/analysis within Fusion to validate structural assumptions.
Document your design rationale, material choices, and manufacturing considerations.
polish_30_36: Prepare clean renders and documentation of both parts.
Prepare your presentation explaining design decisions, especially generative design/topology optimization choices and their rationale.
Review submission requirements carefully, this is likely a documentation/render submission, not a live coding demo.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a clear before/after of your topology-optimized part versus a naive design, demonstrating genuine, quantified weight reduction while maintaining structural requirements, that's the concrete evidence of real design-for-manufacturing skill this challenge is testing for.

strengths: Very clearly specified deliverable structure and tool requirements.
Genuinely completable in 36 hours for a team with real Fusion experience.
weaknesses: Completely inaccessible to a team without genuine CAD/mechanical design skill in this specific tool.
Not comparable in evaluation criteria to the software/hardware-build PS elsewhere in this dataset.

roles_needed: Mechanical/CAD designer with real Autodesk Fusion experience (mandatory)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS is not viable without genuine, hands-on Fusion proficiency on the team, that's a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.
team_fit.approach: Confirm tool proficiency before anything else, this determines whether the PS is even attemptable.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The entire design process, genuine mechanical design and manufacturing-optimization judgment, requires real hands-on CAD skill that AI tooling doesn't substitute for.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Not applicable in the typical sense, but attempting this without real Fusion proficiency (hoping to figure it out on the fly) would almost certainly produce an unconvincing submission.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, this is a design-skill and tool-proficiency challenge.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, if the team lacks Fusion proficiency, this PS should not be selected.

judge_qna.question: How did you apply generative design and topology optimization specifically, and what was the quantified benefit?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific optimization parameters and constraints, and present the measured weight reduction or structural improvement versus a naive baseline design.
judge_qna.follow_up: What manufacturability constraints did you have to balance against pure optimization?

judge_qna.question: How would your chassis and attachment interface actually work in a real warehouse deployment, beyond the CAD model?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Discuss real-world considerations, tolerances, attachment/detachment mechanism, load distribution, that a physical prototype would need to validate beyond the digital design.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest risk in going from your CAD concept to an actual manufactured, working prototype?
